text: The first applicant was born in 1951.
The first applicant lives in Erjovo.
The second applicant is a company incorporated in the Transdniestrian region of Moldova.
The applicants were represented by Mr S.G. Popovschi, a lawyer practising in Tiraspol.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.

The background to the case, including the Transdniestrian armed conflict of 1991-1992 and the subsequent events, is set out in Ilaşcu and Others v. Moldova and Russia ([GC], no. 48787/99, §§ 28-185, ECHR 2004-VII).

The background to the case, including the Transdniestrian armed conflict of 1991-1992 and the subsequent events, is set out in Catan and Others v. the Republic of Moldova and Russia ([GC], nos. 43370/04, 8252/05 and 18454/06, §§ 8-42, ECHR 2012).
On 6 November 2012, the former members of the kolkhoz Rodina from Erjovo and Sarateia villages created the second applicant (a company incorporated in the Transdniestrian region of Moldova).

The second applicant was created with a view to defending the interests of the former members of the kolkhoz Rodina in respect of plans by the Government of the Transdniestrian region of Moldova concerning their land.
On 21 September 2013, the first applicant organised a public meeting for the former members of the kolkhoz Rodina.
The public meeting organised by the first applicant on 21 September 2013 was held with a view to discussing the matter about the land.
Sixty-five persons participated in the public meeting organised by the first applicant on 21 September 2013.
On 23 September 2013, the Rîbniţa District Court imposed a fine of 145 MRT roubles on the first applicant.
The Rîbniţa District Court imposed the fine on the first applicant for breach of the rules of conducting public manifestations.
The Rîbniţa District Court found that the first applicant had not obtained a prior authorisation for holding the public manifestation on 21 September 2013.
The first applicant challenged the Rîbniţa District Court's decision of 23 September 2013 before the MRT (Moldovan Transdniestrian Republic) Supreme Court.
On 31 October 2013, the MRT (Moldovan Transdniestrian Republic) Supreme Court dismissed the first applicant's appeal.
On 31 October 2013, the MRT (Moldovan Transdniestrian Republic) Supreme Court upheld the decision of the Rîbniţa District Court imposing a fine of 145 MRT roubles on the first applicant.

Reports by inter-governmental and non-governmental organisations, the relevant domestic law and practice of the Republic of Moldova, and other pertinent documents were summarised in Mozer v. the Republic of Moldova and Russia ([GC], no. 11138/10, §§ 61-77, 23 February 2016).
